This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e court  following:
 ORDER In Miscellaneous Appeal No.2739/2014, learned counsel for appellants/claimants submits that he has paid deficit Court fee in the appeal filed by the claimants and in support of the said submission,
he has filed a copy of Online Court Fees Cyber Receipt of Rs.7400/- under covering memo,
therefore, the Court fee may be taken on record.
On due consideration, the deficit Court fee is taken on record.

These appeals are filed by M.P. Road Transport Corporation and claimants respectively being aggrieved of award dated 05/09/2014 passed by learned 7th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal in MCC No.1094/2008 on different grounds.

sentences.text: 2. M.P.Road Transport Corporation has taken a ground that bus in question was insured with Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Company Limited, therefore, the onus was on the owner, driver and the insurer of the bus to have paid the compensation.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is submitted that there is a clause in lease agreement dated 08/06/005 executed between the M.P. State Road Transport Corporation and the owner of the bus fastening of liability on the owner of the bus but in violation of the terms and conditions of the agreement, impugned award is passed by learned Claims Tribunal which is liable to be set aside.
3. Learned counsel for the claimants/appellants submits that accident had taken place on 20/04/2008 when Deepak Parashar died in the accident.
The deceased was working as a Salesman in Shiva Tractors.
It is submitted that future prospects etc were not awarded in favour of the applicants, therefore, compensation should have been awarded accordingly.

4. Shri T.S. Lamba, learned counsel for the insurance company, places reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation Vs. Kailash Nath Kothari and others, (1997) 7 SCC 481 wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that definition of owner includes the hirer of the bus namely SRTC which was flying the bus under an agreement on route for which permit was granted in favour of SRTC.

sentences.text:
After hearing learned counsel for the petitioner and going through the record, it is evident that as far as M.P. State Road Transport Corporation is concerned, appeal filed by them seeking to transfer the liability on the owner, insurer is not made out in light of the decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kailash Nath Kothari and others (supra) and eep Devi and others (supra), therefore,
the appeal filed by M.P. State Road Transport Corporation fails and is hereby dismissed.
7.
As far as appeal filed by claimants is concerned, learned Claims Tribunal has considered the income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- per month.
It has made 1/3rd deduction towards living expenses of the deceased, however, it has not added future prospects.
Deceased was working in Shiva Tractors (Farm Tract Company) as a Salesman.

Though there is a income certificate produced by Shri Goldi Khurana but the same has been disbelieved by the Tribunal on account of proper authorisation in favour of Goldi Khurana by the Shiv Tractor Company authorising him to issue said certificate.

Therefore, when annual dependency of the family is taken at Rs.36,000/- and 50% is to be added towards the future prospects and thereafter multiplier of 17 is applied, then total pecuniary compensation will come out to Rs.9,18,000/-.
Over and above which claimants are entitled to Rs.70,000/- under the head of loss of estate, last rites and loss of consortium.
Besides this, claimant No.2-Ku.Sambhavi is entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- under the head of loss of parental consortium.
Thus, total compensation admissible in favour of the claimants will come out to Rs.10,28,000/- in place of Rs.6,87,000/- awarded by learned Claims Tribunal.
Thus, there shall be an enhancement to the tune of Rs.3,41,000/- which will be admissible in favour of the claimants.
8. This additional amount along with accrued interest shall be invested in the name of claimant/claimants in a Monthly Income Scheme of Indian Post Office for a period of six years.
9. In above terms, M.A. No.582/2016 filed by the M.P. State Road Transport Corporation is dismissed and M.A. No.2739/2014 filed by the claimants is disposed of.
9. Record of the Claims Tribunal be sent back immediately.
